name: BarChart
usage:
Comparing amounts across categories (sales per region), ranked lists (horizontal, largest first), parts
of a total over time (stacked)

props.name: data
props.description: The rows: one per category, with a field per series.

props.name: x
props.description:
Field of the rows that holds the category: on the horizontal axis, or on the vertical axis with
`orientation="horizontal"`.

props.name: series
props.description:
The series, in legend order. Colors follow the position in this array (or `slot`), so hiding or filtering a
series never changes the color of the others. A single series uses one color for every bar.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
`vertical`: columns growing up from the horizontal axis; `horizontal`: bars growing right from the vertical
axis, better for long category names or many categories.

props.name: stacked
props.description:
Stacks the series in one bar per category; the end of the bar is the total. Otherwise the series are grouped
side by side.

props.name: showValues
props.description:
Writes the value at the end of each bar (the total for stacked bars). Values that do not fit are left out;
they stay in the tooltip and the table.

props.name: format
props.description: How values are written on the value axis, at the bar ends, in the tooltip and in the table.

props.name: xFormat
props.description: Writes a category, such as a date; by default `String(value)` (dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`).

props.name: xLabel
props.description:
Name of the categories: the header of the first column of the table view. "Category" by default (follows
`locale`).

props.name: emphasis
props.description: Key of the one series the chart is about: it keeps its color and the others use the muted color.

props.name: title
props.description: Title of the chart: what is plotted. It is also the accessible name of the graphic.

props.name: description
props.description: A short description under the title, such as the period or the unit.

props.name: height
props.description:
Height of the graphic in pixels, axis labels included. The states take the same height. The table view starts at
this height and grows with its rows up to 480 px (or this height when it is taller); only longer tables scroll.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Loading: without data, a delayed loading indicator takes the place of the graphic; with data, the previous
graphic stays at reduced opacity until the new data arrives.

props.name: error
props.description: Error: `true` shows the default error state; a node is shown as the message of the error state.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry after an error; shows a "Retry" button in the error state.

props.name: emptyDescription
props.description: Text of the empty state when there is no data, "No data" by default (follows `locale`).

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions in the top-right corner, before the view switch (for example a menu or a time range).

props.name: plain
props.description: Without the card (no background, shadow or padding), for charts inside a Panel, a dialog or a drawer.

fields.name: key
fields.description: Field of the rows that holds the values of this series; also the identity of the series.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name of the series in the legend, the tooltip and the table header; shown as text, never interpreted as HTML.

fields.name: slot
fields.description: Pins the color of the series to a position of the categorical palette (by default its position in the array).

types.name: ValueFormat
types.summary:
How a value is written.
- `'auto'`: in full below 10,000, compact from 10,000 on (1,284 · 12.9K · 4.2M).
- `'number'`: always in full, with grouping separators.
- `'compact'`: always compact.
- `'percent'`: the value is a ratio (0.125 → 12.5%).
- a function: your own formatting (units, currencies).

types.name: ChartXValue
types.summary:
A value of the category field (x): a text, a number or a date. Dates and numbers are written with `xFormat`
(otherwise as `String(value)`).

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Basic usage
examples.description: One series compares a value across categories: every bar has the same color, and the title says what it is.

examples.name: GroupedAndStacked
examples.title: Grouped and stacked
examples.description:
Several series are grouped side by side; `stacked` puts them in one bar per category, whose end is the total.
Neighbors are separated by a 2 px gap, and only the data end is rounded.

examples.name: Horizontal
examples.title: Horizontal and ranked
examples.description:
`orientation="horizontal"` suits long category names and rankings: sort the rows, largest first. `showValues`
writes each value at the end of its bar.

examples.name: Negative
examples.title: Negative values
examples.description: Bars below zero grow down from the baseline and are rounded at their own end.
